title: What is the Bain interview process, and how should you prepare?
description: Bain's hiring steps explained: application, first and second rounds of case and experience interviews, written cases in some offices, and preparation tips.
hook: Candidates often describe Bain's interviewers as friendly and supportive, which helps, but the bar is still high. Here is how Bain's process usually runs and how to prepare for each part.
body:
The steps

  1. Application: CV and cover letter screening, often through campus recruiting for students.
  2. Online test in some offices.
  3. First round: commonly two interviews of about 45 minutes, each with a case and fit questions.
  4. Second round: more interviews with senior people such as managers and partners, sometimes including a written case.
  5. Offer.

The case: candidate-led

Bain cases are usually candidate-led, so you are expected to drive. Bain's preparation pages cover case interviews, experience interviews and other formats, including written cases.

Written cases

Some Bain offices, particularly in Europe and Asia, use a written case in later rounds: you get a pack of slides or data, prepare alone for a set time, then present your recommendation. How to handle written cases.

The experience interview

Expect questions about your background, your motivations and why Bain. Candidates report fit conversations with partners or senior managers about your career and aspirations, so prepare a clear story of where you have been and where you want to go.

How to prepare

  • Do Bain's official practice cases on its interview preparation pages.
  • Practise candidate-led cases where you drive from structure to recommendation.
  • If your office uses written cases, practise reading a data pack quickly and building three or four clear slides.
  • Prepare stories about teamwork and results; Bain's culture places weight on both.

Sources

  • Bain: Case interview preparation
  • IGotAnOffer: Bain case interview
  • PrepLounge: Bain case interview guide
  • Glassdoor: Bain interview reviews

Checked November 2026. Processes change by office and year, so always confirm with the firm's own careers page and your recruiter.
